result.note: Tested the March 2026 and FY26 trade deficit figures and the rise in US-bound exports after the tariff ruling; skipped TBB's analysis of energy imports.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's trade data released in April 2026:
items: India's trade deficit for March 2026 narrowed to a nine-month low of USD 20.67 billion.
India's trade deficit for FY 2025-26 was at a three-year high of USD 119 billion.
In FY 2025-26, India's export growth outpaced its import growth.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because annual imports grew 6.5% while exports grew only 4.22%, which widened the FY26 deficit to USD 119 billion. The March narrowing came mainly from a sharp fall in imports, especially energy.
questions.source: Despite this monthly dip, the financial year 2025-2026 (FY26) deficit sits at a three-year high of USD 119 billion, as annual imports (+6.5%) continue to outpace export growth (+4.22%).

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's exports to the United States in March 2026:
items: Shipments to the US rose 17.4% to USD 8.02 billion.
The rise followed a US Supreme Court ruling that cut punitive tariffs from 50% to 10%.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are correct. The increase was led by textiles and engineering goods after the US Supreme Court ruling reduced the 50% tariffs to 10%, even as exports to the Middle East fell by 57.95%.
questions.source: This surge in textiles and engineering goods follows a US Supreme Court ruling that slashed punitive 50% tariffs down to 10%, which we covered here.
